title: A nationwide nested case-control study indicates an increased risk of acute interstitial nephritis with proton pump inhibitor use
authors: Blank ML, Parkin L, Paul C, Herbison P
followUp: new episodes of PPI use 2005 to 2009
population: New Zealand cohort of 572,661 patients starting a new episode of PPI use without prior interstitial nephritis or renal disease; 72 cases of acute interstitial nephritis (46 confirmed by histology) with 10 matched controls each
funder: Primary financial support was provided by the Health Research Council of New Zealand and Medsafe (grant number 10/031). Additional support was provided to M-LB through a University of Otago Masters' scholarship. The funders had no role in the design of the study, or in the collection, analysis, or interpretation of the data.
authorConflicts: All the authors declared no competing interests.
result: Acute interstitial nephritis resulting in hospitalisation or death: crude incidence 11.98 (95% CI 9.11 to 15.47) per 100,000 person-years during current PPI use against 1.68 (0.91 to 2.86) during past use; matched OR for current against past use 5.16 (2.21 to 12.05) among histologically confirmed cases, similar after adjustment and with probable cases included.
